text:
anya: Heads-up - ran a new pass on GPU mem after last week's OOM spike. Trying a combination of slab compaction + small burst buffers instead of a single large workspace pool. numbers below.

ben: curious, what changed vs the current slab recycling?

anya: two things: 1) compact slabs on allocation pressure instead of periodic sweep (so we reclaim mixed-fragment slabs early). 2) allocate ephemeral "burstpad" buffers for the short-lived KV decode phase, recycled immediately after token emit. this reduces peak workspace by ~18% in our microbench.

maria: any regression on latency p95? we can't shift tails.

anya: p50/p95 unchanged (+0.5ms noise). p99 up by ~3ms on long seqs (3200+) but that's due to extra compaction work during autofocus path. we can defer compaction off the critical path by doing async compaction on idle streams.

ben: can you paste the profiling snippet?

anya: sure:```text
# nvprof summary snippet (kernel time ms)
kernel_select         12.4
kv_decode             8.1
burstpad_alloc        0.9
slab_compact          2.3
total_infer           85.7
```

anya: note: slab_compact is called only on <5% of requests in the test mix, but those coincide with long-context chat which is why p99 moved.

maria: what's the policy for TTL + shard sizing in this experiment? previous tests saw hit-rate drop when shards got too small.

anya: good point. we switched to dynamic shard scaling: base shard size 128MB, scale up to 512MB at >75% occupancy. TTL kept at 48h but we change eviction aggressiveness based on hit-rate: if hit-rate drops >5% we back off compaction for 30m.

ben: that dynamic scaling sounds promising. do we have sim results?

anya: yes - quick sim (10M requests mix):
- fixed 128MB shards, TTL 48h -> avg hit 78.3%, mem 4.9GB
- dynamic shards (128->512) -> avg hit 83.9%, mem 5.6GB peak but fewer cold-misses
- with burstpad + compaction -> peak mem 4.6GB, avg hit 82.7%

maria: tradeoffs look reasonable. the peak mem with dynamic shards is higher but hit-rate improves. burstpad helps bring peak back down.

ci-bot: perf-test: build 2026.03.15-8 completed. regression-checker: no failure, perf delta p99 +2.7ms for long-seq test.

ben: to reduce the p99 impact could we move compaction to a background CUDA stream and limit threads doing compaction?

anya: tried that in a branch — background compaction hides ~70% of the extra work for long seqs, p99 delta drops to +0.9ms. downside: slightly higher transient PCIe traffic and a bit more GPU mem pinned during compaction window.

maria: ok can we run a cluster-wide canary with background compaction + burstpad + dynamic shards for 24h? target: no more than +1.5ms p99 and <=5% extra peak mem across nodes.

anya: yes I'll assemble the canary config. draft config snippet:```yaml
cache:
  base_shard_mb: 128
  max_shard_mb: 512
  scale_threshold: 0.75
  ttl_hours: 48
allocator:
  slab_compact_mode: async
  slab_size_mb: 64
  burstpad_enabled: true
  burstpad_max_mb: 48
  compaction_concurrency: 2
```

ben: also add a metric for "burstpad_reuse_hitrate" and slab_fragmentation_pct so we can correlate.

anya: will add. anyone object to rolling canary tomorrow morning? :+1: or :thinking:?

maria: +1 — schedule after the morning deploy window.

ben: +1 from me.

perf-bot: metric alert rule added: alert if p99(delta) > 1.5ms for 30m or slab_fragmentation_pct increases >10% in 15m.

anya: thanks — I'll post results and the canary ID when it starts.
